0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revisron ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 February 1984, after the draft finalized by the Fire Fishting Sectional Committee had been approved by the CIvil Engineering Division Council.

charactenstics.

0.2 Dry powder used for fighting fires 10 burning metal has special Whereas, dry powder of a particular composition may extinguish fires 1D a particular metal only, others may be employed for extinguishing all types of metal fires. This standard does not, therefore, live the exact constuuents of each type of dry powder. The dry powder is aenerally composed of baSIC material of eutectrc chlorides, ammonium phosphate, diamonium phosphate, sodium chloride or a mixture of sodium chloride with ammonium phosphate with additives to make It water repellant, free flowing and confirming to various requirements mentioned 10 this standard. However, It may be mentioned that chemicals used for the composrtion should not emit any tOXIC or Irritating vapors on meltmg or decomposition. 0.3 This standard was first published In 1968. Thrs revision has been prepared based on the studies conducted by Defence Institute of Fire

Research in respect of performance requirement.
0.4 The dry powder covered by this standard may be applied In one of the following ways, depending upon the Situation a) By scoop/shovel,

b) By filling the powder loosely in plastic bags and placrng the bag over the burning metal, and
c) By USiDI in dry powder extinguisher with applicator for gentle application for powder. 3

IS : 4861 � 1984 0,5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated. expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960�. The number of significant places retained in the rounded otT value should be the same as that of the specified value in this
standard.

1. SCOPE

1.1 This standard Jays down the requirements of dry powder for fighting fires in burning metals only. 2. REQUIREMENTS 2.0 TIle sample of powder for testing shall be drawn in such a way that it represents the entire strata of powder from any container and shall be tested for properties mentioned below.
2.1 AppareDt Denlity - The apparent density of the powder when determined by the method given in 2.1.1 shall be between 0'75 g/m and 1'18 g/ml. 2.1.1 A sample of 100 g of dry powder shall be placed in a clean dry

2S0-ml glass-stoppered graduated cylinder conforming to IS : 878�197St.
The cylinder shall be rotated slowly, end over end, for ten complete

cycles and then set upright to Jet the powder settle for 60 seconds. After shaking it gently to level off the surface of the powder, the volume of the powder in the cylinder shall be Doted and the apparent density calculated as follows:
d . 100 Apparent easlty == Volume of powder 2.2 Partlde Size OlltrlHtloll - The particle size distribution of dry powder shall be such that 100 percent of it PUleS throup 120-I'm IS Sieve, at least 90 percent tbroup 75 "m IS Sieve and Dot more than 10 percent throup 38 "m IS Sieve. For this purpose 100 I of powder shall be used aad the applicable requiremeDt8 of IS : 1607-1977: shall be followed, the duration of lieviDllhal1 be 30 miD for hand sieviDI aad 110

min for machine sieviDIeRules for rOllndina otr Dumerical v.lun ( '1'11_). tSpeci6cation for sradu.ted meuuriDS cyllDden ("'" r."~Io,, ). :Method Cor telt sievinl (/irll rnl,lo" ).

IS: _1-1984
2.3 Hypoacoplcliy ud CaklDl - Separately weigh two dry watchglasses. Place about 5 I of dry powder in each of them and weigh them accurately. Also weigh 100 g of dry powder in a 250-ml beaker, The three samples shall be placed in a desiccator jar containing saturated solution of ammonium chloride in water to produce a relative humidity of 80 percent. The samples in watch-glasses shall be checked for increase in mass after every 7 days for 21 days. The mass should not increase by 0�05 percent at any stage. If this condition is satisfied, then sample in beaker shall be kept in a desiccator containing anhydrous calcium chloride for 2 days and then in a desiccator containing ammonium chloride solution for 2 days and this cycle should be repeated for 20 days. Observe the formation of any caking or lump in the powder. In case there is any caking or Jump formation, allow it to drop from a height of 100 em OD a smooth bard surface. The lump shall be friable to pass the requirements given in 2.2.
2.4 Water RepelleDcJ - Weigh 50 g of dry powder in a tared beaker and gradually fill it with 50 ml of distilled water. After 2 minutes the dry powder and the water from the beaker shall be carefully poured out and the beaker with wet powder, if any, dried in an oven at 60�C for 2 hours and then cooled in a desiccator containing dry calcium chloride for 1 hour. The beaker shall be weighed and the mass of dry residue calculated. The mass of the dry powder residue shall not exceed 0-75 g ( 1-5 percent ).

2.S Free -'10,"81 Characterlltici ( Etllde.t Fluidity) - Transfer 100 g of dry powder to a glass funnel of 7� 5 em diameter with its outlet plugged with thumb. The powder should be released by removing the thumb into a cylindrical flask of 250-ml capacity. The powder should ftow freeJy from the funnel. If this condition is satisfied, then transfer this powder in conical ftask and plug it with a cork. This should be then put in a mechanical vibrator having a frequency of 200 vibrations per minute. Allow it to vibrate for 2 hours and examine its flow again. The powder should flow down smoothly. 2.6 Heat Tilt - Weiah 200 I of dry powder in a tinned steel cup, 75 mm in diameter aDd SO mm deep with a closely fitted cover. Place the cup in a thermostatically COD trolled oven at a temperature of 60�C for a week. The sample shall then be examined for caking or Jump formation. The lump or cake, wben dropped from a height of 100 em on a smooth hard surface, shal) be firable to pass the requirement laid down in 2.2. NOT. - Thi. requirement ensures that tho dry powder is Itable and neither
decompose. at normlt ambient temperature nor any itl additivel melt at aD elevated temperature or 6O-C and hence render the same a n effective extioluiahiDI apDt wbon used in locatioDI baviDI hilher temperatura.

17 Pin Tilt -- A square metal tray shall be used for the test. The tray sball have a base of 1 x 1 m. Three of itl vertical ,ide.

shall be each 55 mm high aDd the fourth side shall be 40 mm high. The tray shall be construeted out of steel plates having a thickness of not less tlian 6 mm, Ita upper edges shall be reinforced by suitable aDgle iron. The reinforcing angle shall be continuous along three equal sides of the tray to produce a turned out flush edge with the top of the tray. The top edgo 10 formed shall be Dot less than 4S mm in width. The tray sball be placed OD a metal stand 10 that its bottom is not leiS than 45 em from the ground. A 2S mm thick layer of dry sand shall be spread uniformly inside the tray so as to cover its bottom completely. Turnings or chips of Soo I magnesium shall be spread over uniformly OD 0-10 ml area in the tray and set alight. When the whole area covered by metal chips turnings is well alight. 2 kg of dry powder shall be applied gently within a period of 60 seconds. The fire should be completely extinguished. Leave it for 30 minutes undisturbed and remove the upper crust. Fire should be considered effectively extinguished if there is DO unburnt powder left over. 3. PACKING 3.1 The f powder 10 be used in the fire extinguisher and for scooping ahall be packed in quantities of 10 kg and 25 kg in plastic baas and SO kg in jute bas. 3.2 The powder for application in plastic baas shall be packed in plastic bagl havmg the following measurement:

a) 300 x 300 mm,
b) 450 X 450 mm, and c) 600 x 600 mm.
3.2.1 The baas chall be filled to three-fourths of their capacity.

3.3 The streqth of the plastic container mentioned in 3.1 and 3.1 .ball be such that DO distortion or failure of the container shall occur when it is kept on a flat surface under a mass of 10 kg. The container shall also Dot disintegrate to any extent when dropped from a height of 1 m OD a concrete surface after beiDI packed. 3.4 The jute bap shall conform to IS : 7406 ( Part 2 ) - 1980�.
